explanation:
[EFFECT] The month of the year has a non-monotonic, arch-shaped effect on predicted hourly bike demand. Winter months — especially January (month 1) and February (month 2) — carry strong negative contributions, meaning the model predicts significantly fewer rentals during those months, all else being equal. Demand climbs through spring and peaks in the summer-to-early-autumn period (roughly months 5 through 9), where contributions are most consistently positive (up to around +0.2 in log space). December (month 12) is mixed: most hours are still positive, but with a wider spread and some negative values, suggesting more variability than the core summer months.

[IMPORTANCE] Month is the **5th most important** feature out of 9, with an importance score of 0.118 — meaningful, but clearly secondary to the hour of the day (0.833), year (0.200), temperature (0.197), and weekday (0.173). It captures seasonal demand cycles that the other features do not fully explain on their own.

[RECOMMENDATION] Plan for markedly higher bike availability and staffing from late spring through early autumn (approximately May–September), and reduce fleet deployment or maintenance windows during the winter months (especially January–February) when the model consistently predicts lower demand.
